mission.title: Install and Configure Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE)
mission.description: This mission guides you through installing the Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE), a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the deployment and management of Kubernetes clusters on Vultr's infrastructure. It provides seamless integration with Vultr's features, such as automatic load balancer provisioning and node management. Key trade-offs include reliance on Vultr's infrastructure and potential costs associated with resource usage.

steps.title: Install the Vultr CLI
steps.description:
The Vultr CLI is necessary for managing your Vultr resources from the command line.

```bash

curl -LO https://github.com/vultr/vultr-cli/releases/download/v1.0.0/vultr-cli_linux_amd64.tar.gz

tar -xzf vultr-cli_linux_amd64.tar.gz

sudo mv vultr-cli /usr/local/bin/

vultr-cli version

```

> Download the latest Vultr CLI
> Extract the downloaded tarball
> Move the CLI to a directory in your PATH
> Verify the installation

steps.title: Create a Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new Kubernetes cluster on Vultr with the specified version and node count.

```bash

vultr-cli k8s create --region 'ewr' --version '1.30' --node-count 3 --plan 'vc2-2c-4gb'

```

> Replace 'ewr' with your preferred region

steps.title: Set Up kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures your kubeconfig file to connect to the newly created Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

vultr-cli k8s kubeconfig --cluster-id <your-cluster-id> > ~/.kube/config

export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config

```

> Replace <your-cluster-id> with the actual cluster ID
> Set the KUBECONFIG environment variable

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This step checks the status of the nodes in your Kubernetes cluster to ensure they are ready.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see all nodes in 'Ready' status

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step sets up additional configurations like autoscaling and monitoring.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/master/cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/vultr/examples/cluster-autoscaler-vultr.yaml

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/monitoring/main/monitoring.yaml

```

> Install the Cluster Autoscaler
> Install monitoring tools

uninstall.title: Delete the Kubernetes Cluster
uninstall.description:
This step will remove the Kubernetes cluster and all associated resources. Be aware that this will result in data loss.

```bash

vultr-cli k8s delete --cluster-id <your-cluster-id>

```

> Replace <your-cluster-id> with the actual cluster ID

uninstall.title: Remove Orphaned Resources
uninstall.description:
This step ensures that any orphaned resources like load balancers or DNS records are cleaned up.

```bash

vultr-cli loadbalancer list

vultr-cli loadbalancer delete --loadbalancer-id <id>

```

> List load balancers to check for any orphaned resources
> Replace <id> with the actual load balancer ID to delete

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Kubernetes Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you have a backup of your data. This step upgrades your cluster to a newer version.

```bash

kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide

vultr-cli k8s upgrade --cluster-id <your-cluster-id> --version '1.31'

kubectl get nodes

```

> Check the status of all pods before upgrade
> Replace <your-cluster-id> with the actual cluster ID
> Verify that all nodes are in 'Ready' status after the upgrade

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates an issue with the kubeconfig or the cluster not being reachable.

**Fix:**
Ensure your kubeconfig is correctly set up and the cluster is running.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'No resources found in default namespace'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that there are no resources deployed in the default namespace.

**Fix:**
Check if you have deployed any applications or switch to the correct namespace.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create load balancer: Invalid API key'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the API key used for Vultr is incorrect or not set.

**Fix:**
Verify your API key and ensure it is correctly configured in your environment.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient capacity in region'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the selected region does not have enough resources available.

**Fix:**
Try creating the cluster in a different region or reduce the node count.
